chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari narrated to me from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad al-Ziyadi from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha who said, 'Aban ibn Uthman narrated to us from Fudayl from Abu Hamza from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:'
Islam is built upon five: upon the Salat, and the Zakat, and the Sawm, and the Hajj, and the Wilayah, and we did not call out with anything as we called out with the Wilayah.
ai.seo_question: What are the five pillars of Islam according to Shia hadith, and how is Wilayah included?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Shia doctrine of 'Tathlith al-Arba'ah' or the inclusion of Wilayah as a foundational pillar alongside the four ritual acts, distinguishing it from Sunni traditions. The Imam emphasizes the unique status of Wilayah by noting that no other concept was proclaimed with such divine intensity, underscoring its role as the spiritual and political axis of the faith. This reflects the Shia belief that obedience to the Ahl al-Bayt is inseparable from the practice of Islam itself.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad Al Ashary narrated to me, from Moalla Bin Muhammad Al Ziyadi, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Al Washa who said, ‘Aban Bin Usman narrated to us, from Fuzayl Bin Abu Hamza, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> having said: ‘

Islām is built upon five – Upon the Salāt, and the Zakāt, and the Soām (Fasts), and the Hajj, and the Wilayah, and weasws do not call (emphasise) with anything like what weasws called (have emphasised) with the Wilayah’.
en.sarwar: 1. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash’ari narrated to me from Mu’ alia ibn Muhammad al-Ziyadi from Hassan ibn Ali al-Washsha’ who has said that narrated to us Aban ibn ‘Uthman from Fudayl from abu Hamza from abu Ja’far (a.s.) who has said the following: “Abu Ja’far (a.s.) has said, ‘

Islam is based on five principles. It is based on Prayer, Charity (al-Zakat) Fasting, Hajj and al-Wilayah (Divine Authority of A ’immah). The call to none of the other principles has been so emphatic as it has been to al-Wilayah.’”
